summary.intent: Plan and run a measurement effort for Caliper's type-correctness accuracy and Storybook first-load performance (accuracy as the gate, speed as the constraint), and clear merge conflicts blocking open PRs.
summary.outcome: Shipped trail 166's three perf branches as PRs #315-#317 and dropped the diagnostics-index branch. Started trail #172 with two workers (reference sample, checker-modes measurement). Resolved conflicts on #312 and #314, so all six open PRs are now MERGEABLE (but BLOCKED, presumably on checks/review).

repo: The weekly record runs a whole-project batch extract, so it does not measure Storybook's first load. The addon uses a lazy session that indexes every file and resolves components on demand.

The oracle that scores Caliper is the TypeScript 7.1 checker, so measuring checker mode against it is circular and a near-100% agreement proves nothing. An independent reference (two-method labelled sample) is needed.

The user treats props surfaced through collapsed or inherited layers as correct; RDT parity is only a reference point. The 'own props, with layers' column (99.3-100% on four corpora) is the headline number, and the 58.2% shadcn-without-layers figure should no longer be quoted.

Perf findings: cloning about 530 diagnostics per component answer is the cost, not scanning them, so a component-diagnostics index gave no gain; sharing diagnostics via Arc would be the real fix. CLI watch's snapshot() deep-copies output (15-20 ms/event on Chakra) while current_output() shares an Arc.
Python script tests in the repo can't be run with `python -I`, which drops the working directory from the import path; the repo has its own test command (71 script tests, 29 oracle tests).
typescript@7.1.0-beta is pinned, so defaulting to checker mode raises a beta-dependency question that needs an ADR.
#312 and #314 conflicted because main had landed `#![deny(missing_debug_implementations)]` in lib.rs and #313 had changed weekly.py; both resolutions kept both sides.

code.finding: watch now publishes session.current_output() (shared Arc) and falls back to snapshot() only before initialize; saves 15-20 ms per event on Chakra.
A publish(next, replaced) helper hands replaced revisions to free_in_background (now pub(super) in revision.rs), cutting eager Chakra edit latency from about 100 ms to 80-88 ms.

Affects-list ids are computed in parallel with rayon, with FNV unchanged and the table fill and collision check serial; saves about 4-6 ms on Chakra serialize, and the canonical JSON digest is identical to main.

workflow: Machine load of 6-13 made absolute timings noisy; interleaved before/after rounds in the same session were used so only same-run differences count.
A user message cut off mid-sentence ('#315–'); verifying actual PR mergeability rather than guessing was the right response.
GitHub mergeability is computed lazily, so it had to be forced and rechecked before concluding which PRs conflicted.
The worker sandbox leaves large scratch data in /tmp/claude-501/t166, which needs manual cleanup.

friction: User messages were truncated or ambiguous (the cut-off PR list and a bare 'docs/core-api-rest'), requiring clarification and a user interrupt.
Mergeability for several PRs showed as still computing, so conflict status had to be polled repeatedly.
My first Python test invocation failed because of the `-I` flag and had to be redone with the repo's own command.
Load on the machine was never quiet during perf measurement, limiting confidence in absolute numbers.
